p: As it is written in the: John goes before Christ as it was foretold by the prophets.
prophets: This is the figure of speech called metonymy, by which is meant the books of the prophets Malachi and Isaiah.
I send my messenger: The prophet uses the present tense when he speaks of a thing to come, as he is as sure of it as if he had already seen it.
before thy face: A metaphor taken from the practice of kings, who used to have ushers go before them.
John did baptize in the wilderness: The sum of John's doctrine, or rather Christ's, is remission of sins and amendment of life.

baptism of repentance for the remission: The Jews used many kinds of washings: but here a peculiar kind of washing is spoken of, which contains within it true baptism, amendment of life, and forgiveness of sins.
And preached: John and all ministers cast their eyes upon Christ the Lord.
stoop down and unloose: The evangelist is expressing here the condition of the basest servant.
baptized you with water: He shows that all the power of baptism proceeds from Christ, who baptizes the inner man.
And it came to pass in: Christ consecrates our baptism in himself.
And straightway: The vocation of Christ from heaven, as head of the Church.
coming up out of the water: John, who went down into the water with Christ.
well pleased: See Geneva "Mt 3:17"
And immediately the Spirit: Christ being tempted overcomes.

driveth him into the wilderness: "Driveth" here does not refer to something violent and forcible: but the divine power clothes Christ (who had lived until this time as a private man) with a new person, and prepares him for the battle that was at hand, and for his ministry.
Now after that John was put: After John is taken Christ shows himself more fully.
Now as he walked by the: The calling of Simon and Andrew.
And when he had gone a: The calling of James and John.
Capernaum: From the city of Nazareth.
And there was in their synagogue: He preaches that doctrine by which alone Satan is driven out of the world, which he also confirms by a miracle.
with an unclean spirit: Literally, "a man in an unclean spirit", that is to say, possessed with an evil spirit.
Jesus of Nazareth: He was born in Bethlehem, but through the error of the people he was called a Nazarene, because he was brought up in Nazareth.
Holy One of God: He alludes to the name that was written in the golden plate which the high Priest wore; Ex 28:36
had torn him: See below, Mr 9:20.
among themselves: As men who were amazed.
commandeth he even the unclean spirits: By his own authority, or as a lord.
round about Galilee: Not only into Galilee, but also into the countries bordering upon it.
And forthwith: By healing different diseases he shows that he has brought true life into the world.
For it is not proper for the demons to preach the gospel; Ac 16:18
next towns: Villages which were like cities.
And there came a leper to: By healing the leprous he shows that he came for this reason: to wipe out the sins of the world with his touch.
And saith unto him: He shows that he was not motivated by ambition, but only by the desire for his Father's glory, and by his love towards poor sinners.
priest: All the posterity of Aaron had the authority to judge a leper.
